24	## 1. Claude Code 能否自动把 session 对话和操作日志记录到项目 `logs/xxx.md`？
25	
26	**部分支持，但需要你自己用 hooks / export 脚本落地。**
27	
28	Claude Code 官方会持续保存 session，本地 transcript 默认在：
29	
30	```text
31	~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl
32	```
33	
34	也可以在会话里用 `/export` 把当前 conversation 保存为纯文本文件；官方文档还说明这些本地 session 文件默认 30 天后清理，可通过配置调整。([Claude Code][1])
35	
36	但是，**Claude Code 默认不会自动把完整对话保存到当前 repo 的 `logs/` 目录**。要做到这一点，推荐用 hooks。Claude Code hooks 能在 `SessionStart`、`UserPromptSubmit`、`PreToolUse`、`PostToolUse`、`Stop`、`SubagentStart/Stop`、`TaskCreated/Completed`、`SessionEnd` 等生命周期事件触发；hook 输入里包含 `session_id`、`cwd`、`transcript_path` 等信息。([Claude Code][2])
37	
38	你项目里其实已经有一个基础版本：`audit_event.py` 会从 hook stdin 读取 JSON payload，然后写到当前项目的 `.agent/audit/tool-events.jsonl`，字段包括 `timestamp`、`hook_event_name`、`tool_name`、`session_id`、`cwd` 和完整 payload。 这说明你的项目已经具备 **tool-event audit log**，但还没有完整的 **conversation transcript mirror / session summary log**。
39	
40	我建议分三层做：
41	
42	```text
43	.agent/audit/
44	  tool-events.jsonl              # raw hook events, 默认不提交或只提交 sanitized 样例
45	
46	logs/claude-sessions/
47	  <date>-<session-id>.jsonl       # transcript mirror，可选，不建议默认 commit
48	  <date>-<session-id>.summary.md  # curated session summary，可 review 后 commit
49	
50	docs/handoffs/
51	  m9-handoff.md
52	  m10-handoff.md                  # milestone 级别核心记忆，应该 commit
53	```
54	
55	关键安全建议：**不要默认把完整 transcript commit 到 GitHub**。Claude session 里可能包含本地路径、命令输出、错误日志、环境变量片段、PR 链接、甚至误打印的 secret。更好的做法是：
56	
57	```text
58	raw logs:
59	  .agent/audit/**
60	  logs/claude-sessions/raw/**
61	  默认 .gitignore
62	
63	curated memory:
64	  PROJECT_STATE.md
65	  docs/handoffs/*.md
66	  docs/adr/*.md
67	  docs/meeting-notes/*.md
68	  docs/evidence/*.md
69	  review 后 commit
70	```
71	
72	可以让 Claude Code 加一个 skill：
73	
74	```text
75	.claude/skills/session-closeout/SKILL.md
76	```
77	
78	用途是每次长任务结束后生成：
79	
80	```text
81	- What changed
82	- Files changed
83	- Tests run
84	- Decisions made
85	- Open questions
86	- Follow-up issues to create
87	- Memory updates proposed
88	```
89	
90	然后由 human 批准后更新 `PROJECT_STATE.md`、`docs/handoffs/`、ADR 或 GitHub issue。

94	## 2. Claude Code 支持 GitHub webhook 吗？能否响应 PR review / comments / labels？
95	
96	**支持几种不同层级，但要区分 “GitHub Actions 触发新 agent run” 和 “push 事件进入正在运行的本地 session”。**
97	
98	### 方案 A：GitHub Actions + `@claude`，最稳
99	
100	你现在已经有 `.github/workflows/claude.yml`，它监听：
101	
102	```yaml
103	issue_comment:
104	  types: [created]
105	pull_request_review_comment:
106	  types: [created]
107	issues:
108	  types: [opened, assigned]
109	pull_request_review:
110	  types: [submitted]
111	```
112	
113	并且只有 comment / issue / review body 包含 `@claude` 时才运行 Claude Code Action。 官方文档也确认 Claude Code GitHub Actions 可以通过 PR/issue 中的 `@claude` 触发，分析代码、创建 PR、实现功能和修 bug，并且 action 是基于 Claude Agent SDK 构建的。([Claude Code][3])
114	
115	这适合：
116	
117	```text
118	@claude review this PR
119	@claude implement issue #123
120	@claude summarize unresolved review comments
121	@claude update docs based on this decision
122	```
123	
124	如果你想让它更新 issue comments / labels / PR comments，workflow 权限需要从 read 扩到 write，例如：
125	
126	```yaml
127	permissions:
128	  contents: write
129	  pull-requests: write
130	  issues: write
131	  actions: read
132	  id-token: write
133	```
134	
135	但我建议分 workflow：
136	
137	```text
138	claude.yml
139	  手动 @claude 响应，允许 contents/pull-requests/issues write
140	
141	claude-code-review.yml
142	  自动 PR review，默认只读或只写 review comment
143	
144	issue-triage.yml
145	  label/comment triage，issues: write，但不改代码
146	
147	labels-sync.yml
148	  只同步 .github/labels.yml，需要人工 workflow_dispatch
149	```
150	
151	工程实践文档里的 AI pickup rule 很适合这里：implementation agent 只能处理 open issue、带 `ai:ready`、决策已 `decision:confirmed`、有 acceptance criteria、无 `ai:blocked`，且不涉及 secrets/破坏性 migration/生产 infra/客户可见副作用，除非 human 明确批准。
152	
153	### 方案 B：Claude Code Routines + GitHub trigger，云端事件触发
154	
155	Claude Code Routines 支持 schedule、API trigger、GitHub event trigger，运行在 Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure；GitHub trigger 会在匹配事件发生时启动一个新 session。([Claude Code][4]) 官方文档说明 GitHub triggers 当前支持 PR 和 release 两类事件，PR 事件包括 opened、closed、assigned、labeled、synchronized 等；每个匹配事件都会启动独立 session，不复用之前的 session。([Claude Code][4])
156	
157	这适合：
158	
159	```text
160	PR labeled ai:ready → 新 cloud session 生成 plan
161	PR updated → 自动 review diff
162	release created → 生成 release notes / readiness report
163	nightly → issue backlog grooming
164	```
165	
166	但它不适合保存“一个长期本地 session 的连续上下文”，因为每个 GitHub event 是新 session。你的 repo memory 仍然要靠 GitHub 文件和 issue/PR 记录。
167	
168	### 方案 C：Claude Code Channels，把 webhook 推进正在运行的本地 session
169	
170	Claude Code Channels 是另一类东西：它允许 MCP server 把 messages、alerts、webhooks 推入一个正在运行的 Claude Code session。官方说它可用于 CI results、chat messages、monitoring events，让 Claude 在你离开终端时也能反应；这是 research preview，需要 Claude Code v2.1.80+，并且 session 启动时要用 `--channels` opt-in。([Claude Code][5]) Channels reference 说明 channel 本质是 MCP server，通过 `notifications/claude/channel` 把外部事件送进 Claude Code session，可做 one-way webhook 或 two-way chat bridge。([Claude Code][6])
171	
172	这适合：
173	
174	```text
175	GitHub webhook → local channel server → active Arch Claude session
176	CI failed → Claude sees event immediately
177	Issue label changed → Claude receives payload
178	PR review submitted → Claude receives payload and responds
179	```
180	
181	但它更复杂，且是 research preview。我建议你的路线是：
182	
183	```text
184	短期：
185	  GitHub Actions @claude + issue labels/comments
186	
187	中期：
188	  Routines 处理 cloud-side GitHub event automation
189	
190	高级：
191	  Channels 将 selected GitHub webhook 推入正在运行的 Arch session
192	```

196	## 3. 如何从 GitHub comments 中提取需求确认/设计变更并沉淀为核心记忆？
197	
198	这件事不能让 Claude “看到评论就直接改 PROJECT_STATE”。应该用 **两阶段 memory promotion**：
199	
200	```text
201	GitHub comment/review/label event
202	  ↓
203	Issue Triage / Decision Extractor agent
204	  ↓
205	生成 proposed memory patch
206	  ↓
207	human review
208	  ↓
209	更新核心记忆文件
210	```
211	
212	我建议新增这些文件：
213	
214	```text
215	.claude/agents/github-decision-extractor.md
216	.claude/agents/github-issue-triage.md
217	.claude/agents/pr-review-followup.md
218	
219	.claude/skills/github-comment-distill/SKILL.md
220	.claude/skills/memory-promotion/SKILL.md
221	.claude/skills/pr-closeout-review/SKILL.md
222	```
223	
224	`github-comment-distill` 的职责：
225	
226	```text
227	输入：
228	  issue/PR comments, review comments, labels, PR diff, linked task doc
229	
230	输出：
231	  confirmed_requirements:
232	  changed_requirements:
233	  confirmed_design_decisions:
234	  changed_design_decisions:
235	  open_questions:
236	  blockers:
237	  proposed_labels:
238	  proposed_core_memory_patch:
239	```
240	
241	`memory-promotion` 的职责：
242	
243	```text
244	只生成 patch，不直接 claim truth：
245	- PROJECT_STATE.md patch
246	- docs/adr/xxxx.md draft
247	- docs/tasks/Mx-Txxx.md update
248	- docs/handoffs/mx-handoff.md update
249	- GitHub issue comment summary
250	```
251	
252	沉淀规则建议：
253	
254	```text
255	comment 只是 evidence，不自动成为 truth
256	label decision:confirmed + human 明确 wording 才能进入 ADR / PROJECT_STATE
257	模糊评论 → decision:needed + ai:blocked
258	实现细节 → task doc / PR closeout
259	长期架构决策 → ADR
260	milestone 状态 → PROJECT_STATE / docs/milestones.md
261	```
262	
263	这和你的工程实践文档一致：Issue Triage Agent 可以读 comments 并识别问题是否已解决，但不能从模糊评论推断决策；Implementation Agent 只能在确认后的 issue 上工作。

267	## 4. agents/skills 如何迁移到别的项目？
268	
269	**不要直接无脑复制到目标项目根目录。最佳方式是“staging → audit → adapt → install”。**
270	
271	Claude Code skills 是文件系统 artifact，项目级 skills 放在：
272	
273	```text
274	.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
275	```
276	
277	个人级 skills 放在：
278	
279	```text
280	~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md
281	```
282	
283	官方文档说明 project skills 只对当前项目生效，personal skills 对所有项目生效，plugin skills 通过 plugin namespace 生效；skills 的 body 只在使用时加载，适合把重复流程从 `CLAUDE.md` 中拆出来。([Claude Code][7]) Agent SDK 也支持从 `.claude/skills/`、`~/.claude/skills/` 或 plugin 路径发现 filesystem skills。([Claude Code][8])
284	
285	我建议采用四层复用模型：
286	
287	### A. 通用、无项目耦合：做成 personal skill 或内部 plugin
288	
289	例如：
290	
291	```text
292	pr-closeout-review
293	github-comment-distill
294	session-closeout
295	ci-failure-triage
296	test-coverage-review
297	```
298	
299	可以放：
300	
301	```text
302	~/.claude/skills/
303	```
304	
305	或建立一个内部 repo：
306	
307	```text
308	kca-agent-pack/
309	  skills/
310	  agents/
311	  hooks/
312	  templates/
313	  README.md
314	```
315	
316	然后每个项目通过 submodule/subtree 或脚本安装。
317	
318	### B. 项目相关但可复用：先放 staging
319	
320	目标项目里先放：
321	
322	```text
323	.agent-import-staging/kca-agent-pack/
324	```
325	
326	然后让 Claude Code 执行：
327	
328	```text
329	Analyze .agent-import-staging/kca-agent-pack.
330	For each skill/agent:
331	- classify as reusable / needs adaptation / reject
332	- identify project-specific assumptions
333	- identify commands, paths, labels, policies to rewrite
334	- propose final installation path
335	Do not install until plan is approved.
336	```
337	
338	再迁移到：
339	
340	```text
341	.claude/skills/
342	.claude/agents/
343	docs/agent-practices/
344	```
345	
346	### C. 强项目耦合：不要迁移，只迁移理念
347	
348	例如 KCA 专用的 Kaggle approval、competition artifact layout、Supabase schema agent，不适合直接复制到普通 SaaS 项目。应该抽象出：
349	
350	```text
351	approval-gate-review
352	artifact-ledger
353	remote-side-effect-policy
354	```
355	
356	### D. 带脚本的 skills：必须安全审计
357	
358	官方 Agent Skills 文档提醒，Skills 可以包含指令和代码，恶意 Skill 可能诱导 Claude 执行不符合预期的工具或代码，所以只应使用可信来源的 skills。([Claude Platform][9]) 所以迁移时要检查：
359	
360	```text
361	- 是否调用 curl/wget/bash remote code
362	- 是否读取 .env / ssh / cloud credentials
363	- 是否 git push / deploy / delete
364	- 是否写绝对路径
365	- 是否假设某个 repo layout
366	- 是否修改 permissions/hooks
367	```

371	## 5. 产品 release 后是否还依赖 Claude Code？agents/skills/commands 底层调用什么？
372	
373	**KCA 产品 release 后不应该依赖 Claude Code CLI/desktop 本身。** Claude Code 是开发工具；KCA runtime 应该是你自己的 platform worker。
374	
375	你现在项目文档已经把两类 agent 区分得很清楚：Claude Code/VS Code/Desktop/Web 是 platform-development coding agents；runtime competition code agents 是平台内部启动的 agent，初始方向是 Claude Agent SDK、隔离 workspace/container、Kaggle Python/notebook-first、未来 model router 支持 Claude、GPT-style、local vLLM/Ollama 等。
376	
377	更进一步，你当前 M3 里已经把 runtime agent 方向改成了 provider-agnostic：`litellm.completion()` 作为统一 LLM provider interface，Claude、GPT-4o、本地 vLLM/Ollama 可按 job 选择。 这说明 KCA runtime **不是锁死在 Anthropic 模型上**。
378	
379	不过要分清楚几种能力来源：
380	
381	```text
382	Claude Code CLI skills/agents/hooks:
383	  用于开发 KCA repo；依赖 Claude Code。
384	
385	KCA .kca/skills or tools:
386	  你自己定义的产品 runtime skills/tools；不依赖 Claude Code。
387	
388	Claude Agent SDK:
389	  可以作为一种 runtime harness，提供 Claude Code-like agent loop、工具执行、context management。
390	
391	LiteLLM / OpenAI-compatible / vLLM / Ollama:
392	  可以作为 model provider；你要自己实现 tool loop 或通过 KCA worker adapter 接入。
393	
394	KCA commands:
395	  例如 kca run, kca decision, kca kaggle, kca skill；
396	  release 后就是你的产品 CLI/runtime API，不应该依赖 Claude Code。
397	```
398	
399	官方 Claude Agent SDK 的定位是“把 Claude Code 作为 library 构建生产 AI agents”，它提供相同的 tools、agent loop、context management，并且适合 CI/CD、custom applications、production automation。([Claude Code][10]) 但如果你使用 Agent SDK，它主要还是 Claude/Anthropic provider 体系；如果要接 vLLM/Ollama/OpenAI，你需要通过 KCA 的 model router / LiteLLM 路线来承接。
400	
401	我的建议：
402	
403	```text
404	产品 runtime 层：
405	  KCA Worker API
406	    - job runner
407	    - permission policy
408	    - tool executor
409	    - audit/event log
410	    - model router
411	    - GitHub adapter
412	    - Kaggle adapter
413	
414	可插拔 agent backend：
415	  - Claude Agent SDK backend
416	  - LiteLLM tool-loop backend
417	  - OpenAI Responses/Codex backend
418	  - Local vLLM/Ollama backend
419	```
420	
421	这样你可以先用 Claude Agent SDK 获得强 agentic coding 能力，后面逐步替换或混合其他模型。
422

425	## 6. 如何让 Claude Code 在 plan/design/architect 阶段更主动发现问题、提问和 debate？
426	
427	你观察得很对：Claude Code 有时会“按字面完成任务”，不会主动追问隐藏需求。例如你让它接手 `kkr.py/kkr.yaml`，它没有主动发现“多 Kaggle 账户提交”这种重要历史设计理念。其实你的 legacy 工具里已经有不少信号：`kkr.py` 支持 `--env` 覆盖 selected owner 的 dotenv path，`RunManifest` 里有 `owner`、`slug`、`env_path`，`kkr.yaml` 里也出现多个 Kaggle owner/kernel id，例如 `harrysun2006`、`firefly2006`。  
428	
429	要提高主动性，我建议建立一个 **Discovery / Debate Gate**，不是只靠“plan mode”。
430	
431	### 做法 1：每个迁移 legacy 的任务先跑 “design archaeology”
432	
433	新增 skill：
434	
435	```text
436	.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md
437	```
438	
439	要求 Claude 在实现前必须输出：
440	
441	```text
442	Legacy design archaeology:
443	1. What workflows does the legacy tool support?
444	2. What hidden assumptions exist?
445	3. What user personas/accounts exist?
446	4. What side effects exist?
447	5. What state files/registries exist?
448	6. What config dimensions exist?
449	7. Which features should be preserved?
450	8. Which features should be deprecated?
451	9. What questions must be asked before implementation?
452	10. What tests prove behavior parity?
453	```
454	
455	对 `kkr.py/kkr.yaml` 这种任务，强制它先识别：
456	
457	```text
458	- multi-account / owner / env mapping
459	- kernel push vs competition submit
460	- notebook submit vs local file submit
461	- run registry
462	- version labels
463	- fetch/watch/status/list lifecycle
464	- dry-run behavior
465	- H100 / docker_image / Kaggle metadata patch notes
466	```
467	
468	### 做法 2：在 task template 里加入 “assumption challenge”
469	
470	每个 architecture task 的 prompt 里固定加：
471	
472	```text
473	Before proposing implementation, challenge the task:
474	- What important requirement might be hidden in legacy files?
475	- What would break for an expert user?
476	- What design questions should be asked?
477	- What should be preserved even if not mentioned?
478	- What is the minimal reversible implementation?
479	- Give at least 3 alternative designs and argue tradeoffs.
480	```
481	
482	### 做法 3：增加反方 agent
483	
484	新增 agents：
485	
486	```text
487	.claude/agents/requirements-skeptic.md
488	.claude/agents/legacy-archaeologist.md
489	.claude/agents/design-red-team.md
490	```
491	
492	`requirements-skeptic` 不写代码，只问问题。
493	`legacy-archaeologist` 只读 legacy scripts/configs，提取设计理念。
494	`design-red-team` 反驳当前方案，指出丢失能力和长期成本。
495	
496	### 做法 4：把“询问 human”变成 acceptance criteria
497	
498	例如：
499	
500	```text
501	Acceptance criteria:
502	- The agent identified at least 5 legacy behavior dimensions.
503	- The agent listed preserved / changed / dropped behaviors.
504	- The agent asked human for unresolved design decisions unless all are explicitly answered by docs/tests.
505	- No implementation starts until hidden assumptions are documented.
506	```
507	
508	这比“请主动一点”有效，因为它把主动性变成可检查输出。
509	
510	---
511	
512	## 7. 你现在这些实践之外，还能怎么提高开发效率和准确率？
513	
514	你已经有一套很强的 workflow：
515	
516	```text
517	milestones/tasks + worktrees
518	Arch Linux Claude Code --bg 长跑
519	Mac VS Code 做短任务/review
520	mobile app remote control 批准/回答
521	GitHub issues/PR/comments/labels 作为第二交互界面
522	```
523	
524	我建议补齐下面 12 个实践。
525	
526	### 1. 给每个 task 增加 “evidence bundle”
527	
528	每个 PR 必须产出：
529	
530	```text
531	docs/evidence/<task-id>/
532	  closeout.md
533	  commands-run.txt
534	  test-results.md
535	  screenshots-or-traces-index.md
536	  decisions.md
537	```
538	
539	PR body 链接 evidence。工程实践文档也建议 logs 要总结到 issue，并把长期证据放在 `docs/evidence/` 或 GitHub artifact 中。
540	
541	### 2. 建立 “no silent memory” 机制
542	
543	每次 Claude Code 结束时强制问：
544	
545	```text
546	Does this task change project memory?
547	- no
548	- yes: propose patch to PROJECT_STATE.md / ADR / task doc / handoff
549	```
550	
551	只有 human approve 后才更新。
552	
553	### 3. 增加 PR Closeout bot
554	
555	每个 PR 自动检查：
556	
557	```text
558	- linked issue
559	- acceptance criteria checked
560	- tests run
561	- docs updated or not needed
562	- migrations/RLS/secrets impact
563	- remote side effects
564	- evidence link
565	```
566	
567	你的 engineering details 里已经建议 `pr-closeout-check.yml` 用于检查 PR body 是否包含 tests/docs/inventory/closeout links。
568	
569	### 4. 将 “labels” 变成状态机，而不只是标签
570	
571	建议状态流：
572	
573	```text
574	ai:triage
575	  → decision:needed + ai:blocked
576	  → decision:confirmed
577	  → ai:ready
578	  → ai:implementing
579	  → PR opened
580	  → review
581	  → merged / follow-up issues
582	```
583	
584	禁止：
585	
586	```text
587	ai:ready + decision:needed
588	ai:ready + ai:blocked
589	ai:implementing without owner/branch
590	```
591	
592	### 5. 引入 “issue-to-branch naming convention”
593	
594	例如：
595	
596	```text
597	issue #123
598	branch: claude/issue-123-short-title
599	worktree: .worktrees/issue-123-short-title
600	PR title: [#123] Short title
601	```
602	
603	这样 GitHub event、Claude session、worktree、logs、evidence 都能对齐。
604	
605	### 6. 为 Claude Code session 命名
606	
607	Claude Code 支持命名、resume、branch session；session picker 可以按当前 repo/worktree/branch 查找，并且可以导出 transcript。([Claude Code][1]) 你的长跑命令应统一：
608	
609	```bash
610	claude --bg \
611	  --name "M9-T002-spaceship-baseline-issue-123" \
612	  ...
613	```
614	
615	然后 log/evidence 也用同名 ID。
616	
617	### 7. 用 Channels 或 Remote Control 做“响应式开发”，但不要替代 GitHub Actions
618	
619	Remote Control 适合你现在用 mobile app 远程接管本地 session；官方说明 Remote Control 让本地 Claude Code session 继续运行在你的机器上，Web/mobile 只是窗口，适合从手机继续本地任务。([Claude Code][11])
620	
621	Channels 更适合把外部 webhook 推入本地 session。我的建议：
622	
623	```text
624	Remote Control:
625	  人主动介入、批准、回答问题。
626	
627	GitHub Actions:
628	  repo-native 事件、@claude、issue/PR 协作。
629	
630	Channels:
631	  高级事件流，例如 CI failed / PR labeled / issue assigned 推入正在跑的 Arch session。
632	```
633	
634	### 8. 让 KCA 自己 dogfood GitHub interface
635	
636	KCA 产品本身未来要能操作 GitHub，所以现在开发 KCA 时就用同一套抽象：
637	
638	```text
639	GitHub issue/comment/label event
640	  → KCA event adapter
641	  → decision extractor
642	  → job queue
643	  → worker/session
644	  → PR/comment/label update
645	  → audit log
646	```
647	
648	这样你不是“额外做 GitHub automation”，而是在 dogfood 产品核心能力。
649	
650	### 9. legacy migration 要有 behavior parity tests
651	
652	对 `kkr.py/kkr.yaml`，不要只迁移代码。要建立：
653	
654	```text
655	tests/fixtures/kkr/
656	  kkr.yaml
657	  minimal_notebook.ipynb
658	  fake_kaggle_api.json
659	
660	tests/test_kkr_parity.py
661	```
662	
663	覆盖：
664	
665	```text
666	- push --dry-run
667	- submit --dry-run
668	- watch/status/list/fetch parsing
669	- multi-owner env selection
670	- notebook vs local submit
671	- version label / registry behavior
672	```
673	
674	`kkr.py` 已经有 dry-run、JSON output、本地 registry、watch/status/list/fetch 等能力，适合做 parity suite。
675	
676	### 10. 对高风险任务使用双 agent review
677	
678	例如：
679	
680	```text
681	Agent A: implement
682	Agent B: review only
683	Agent C: test coverage reviewer
684	Human: final decision
685	```
686	
687	工程实践文档本身已经把 Inventory Drift Auditor、Issue Triage Agent、Implementation Planner、Implementation Agent、Milestone Reviewer、Test Coverage Reviewer、Release Readiness Agent 分成不同职责，并规定各自不能越权。
688	
689	### 11. 给 runtime worker 增加 replay
690	
691	每个 job 都能：
692	
693	```bash
694	kca job replay <job_id> --from-event <n> --dry-run
695	```
696	
697	这样当 agent 做错时，你可以复现：
698	
699	```text
700	input prompt
701	model/provider
702	tools allowed
703	tool calls
704	policy decisions
705	files changed
706	test results
707	human decisions
708	```
709	
710	M7 的目标里已经有 “permission policy resolves allow/ask/deny” 和 “audit log records every tool execution with policy decision”。 建议把它升级成可 replay 的 event sourcing。
711	
712	### 12. 明确 M9 前的 readiness gate
713	
714	你的 milestones 里 M9 是第一次真实 Kaggle end-to-end regression：Spaceship Titanic，目标是通过审批 gate 执行一次真实 `kaggle competitions submit` 并记录 public LB score。 所以 M9 前一定要 gate：
715	
716	```text
717	- CI green
718	- dry-run path green
719	- Kaggle credentials verified without printing
720	- submission.csv schema validated
721	- approval gate manually tested
722	- rollback / stop criteria documented
723	- logs/evidence path confirmed
724	```
725

845	## 总结建议
846	
847	你现在的方向是对的，但下一步要把“经验性流程”固化成产品机制：
848	
849	```text
850	Claude Code 开发侧：
851	  hooks + session closeout + GitHub Actions/Routines/Channels + agents/skills
852	
853	KCA runtime 侧：
854	  event log + model router + GitHub adapter + approval gate + replay + evidence bundle
855	
856	共同核心：
857	  GitHub repo 是 source of truth
858	  raw logs 不等于 memory
859	  human-confirmed decisions 才进入 PROJECT_STATE / ADR / milestones
860	```
861	
862	最优先做的不是 M9 继续堆功能，而是 **M8.6：session memory、GitHub event interface、legacy design archaeology、agent/skill reuse packaging**。这会直接提高后续 M9/M10 的开发效率和准确率。

1	# kaggle-code-agent Milestones
2	
3	Status: M0–M9 done; M10 in planning (authorized CTF/lab workflow)  
4	Created: 2026-05-16  
5	Scope: hybrid human + AI code competition platform
6	
7	## Product thesis
8	
9	`kaggle-code-agent` is a platform for human users to collaborate with AI code agents on code competitions and authorized challenge environments.
10	
11	Initial focus: Kaggle competitions.  
12	Later extensions: authorized CTF/lab challenges, Devpost, hackathons, benchmark competitions, and other policy-scoped coding contests.
13	
14	The platform should help a human user:
15	
16	- discuss ideas and strategies;
17	- research competition rules, data, notebooks, papers, discussions, and baseline approaches;
18	- create, modify, test, and iterate code;
19	- track experiments, artifacts, results, submissions, and analysis;
20	- require human approval for external side effects such as Kaggle submissions or remote kernel pushes;
21	- summarize learnings and produce final writeups.
22	
23	## Source of truth
24	
25	**GitHub repo + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations.**
26	
27	All product source code, migrations, tests, architecture decisions, and task specs live in this repository. AI tools do not share hidden memory reliably across sessions or products. Claude Code is the primary development environment for all layers: CLI, backend, UI shell, and worker.
28	
29	Lovable may be used for visual prototyping or landing-page mockups only. It is not the source of truth for schema, migrations, agent runners, or any backend logic.
30	
31	## Terminology: two meanings of "code agent"
32	
33	This project uses two related but distinct agent concepts.
34	
35	### 1. Platform-development coding agents
36	
37	These are external AI tools used to build this repository.
38	
39	Examples:
40	
41	- Claude Code CLI / VS Code / Desktop / Web (primary);
42	- ChatGPT Pro / Cursor (supplementary);
43	- GitHub Actions / Claude Code Web / Routines for cloud automation.
44	
45	Role:
46	
47	- write and review this product's source code;
48	- update docs, tasks, tests, and architecture decisions;
49	- run local tests and CI repair loops;
50	- open branches/PRs under human supervision.
51	
52	Important rule: these tools do not share hidden memory reliably. GitHub repository files are the durable source of truth.
53	
54	### 2. Runtime competition code agents
55	
56	These are agents launched by the finished platform to help a human user compete.
57	
58	Initial runtime direction:
59	
60	- Claude Agent SDK as the first core worker/harness;
61	- isolated workspace/container per job;
62	- Python/notebook-first for Kaggle;
63	- TypeScript/Python service boundary depending on platform vs worker needs;
64	- future model router for Claude, GPT-style models, local vLLM/Ollama models, and specialized tools.
65	
66	Runtime agents must operate under competition-specific policy, sandboxing, budget limits, approval gates, and audit logging.
67	
68	## Architecture north star
69	
70	```text
71	Human user / future UI
72	        ↓
73	TypeScript-first platform/control plane
74	  - project/session/job/task queue
75	  - policy and approval gates
76	  - discussion/research/analysis records
77	  - experiment/run/submission/artifact records
78	  - model router configuration
79	        ↓
80	Worker layer
81	  - Python-first Kaggle workers
82	  - Claude Agent SDK runtime sessions
83	  - notebooks/scripts/tools/kca wrappers
84	  - Playwright/browser/research tools
85	  - sandboxed execution and evaluation
86	        ↓
87	External systems
88	  - GitHub repo / branches / PRs
89	  - Supabase DB/storage/edge functions later
90	  - Kaggle API/CLI, only with approval for remote side effects
91	  - authorized CTF/lab/hackathon platforms under explicit policy
92	```
93	
94	## Cross-cutting rules
95	
96	- GitHub repo files are the project memory and source of truth.
97	- Each agent task gets a branch/worktree/PR when it modifies code.
98	- Main branch remains stable and protected.
99	- Do not allow multiple AI sessions to edit the same branch/files at the same time.
100	- No secrets in repo, prompts, logs, artifacts, or screenshots.
101	- Kaggle submissions, kernel pushes, dataset uploads, and other remote side effects require explicit human approval.
102	- CTF/lab work must be local/sandboxed or explicitly authorized.
103	- Every task prompt should include acceptance criteria and a stop condition.
104	- Every worker loop should have budget, turn, time, and side-effect limits.
105	- Tests and local validation should run before external submission.
106	
107	## Milestone final-review protocol
108	
109	After every milestone final review, before marking done:
110	
111	1. Update `PROJECT_STATE.md` — set current milestone, summarize open decisions, and record any new known blockers.
112	2. Update `README.md` current milestone section to name the new active milestone and goal.
113	3. Update `docs/milestones.md` — mark the finished milestone `✓ done`, add a one-line summary of what landed, and note any follow-ups carried forward.
114	4. Write `docs/handoffs/m{x}-handoff.md` — a per-milestone, ready-to-paste context prompt for the next AI tool / session that will start M{x+1}. Use `docs/handoff-prompt.md` as the canonical template; populate the "State at handoff", "Read these files first", and "Current task" sections from the M{x} final review and the M{x+1} entry in this file. The generic `docs/handoff-prompt.md` stays as the template; the per-milestone instances live under `docs/handoffs/`.
115

367	## M7: KCA CLI architecture — command / skill / tool / job / permission policy ✓ done
368	
369	_Shipped 2026-05-21: four-layer CLI scaffold (command/skill/tool/job), skill loader, tool registry (16 tools), three permission profiles, `kca skill list/show/run` + `kca tool list/audit/doctor`, four seed skills, audit JSONL, 15 smoke tests, and `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md`. 28/28 exit checks PASS — see `docs/m7-final-review.md`._
370	
371	Goal: implement the full KCA command/skill/tool/job architecture so the platform
372	has a stable, inspectable CLI that can drive agent workflows, replace ad-hoc
373	`python tools/kca/kca.py` calls, and enforce structured permission decisions.
374	
375	This is distinct from the product UI shell (M8): M7 is operator/developer-facing
376	and headless. The UI in M8 will call into the same CLI/API surface.
377	
378	See `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-21-r1.md` §1–3 for full design rationale.
379	
380	### Four-layer model
381	
382	| Layer | Description |
383	|---|---|
384	| **Command** | Deterministic CLI/API entry points for operators (`kca job run`, `kca decision approve`). |
385	| **Skill** | Agent-facing workflow recipes stored under `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter. Callable via `kca skill run <name>` or slash-style invocation. |
386	| **Tool** | Executable actions with input/output schema, timeout, permission label, sandbox metadata, and audit logging. |
387	| **Job** | Durable records that run a skill through the agent loop with budget, turn, cost, runtime limits, and decision gates. |
388	
389	### M7 task sequence
390	
391	| Task | Description | Depends on |
392	|---|---|---|
393	| M7-T000 | Audit + repair `.github/workflows/` — fix failing CI checks, add no-db + lint jobs | — |
394	| M7-T001 | Skill loader: read `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter; argument substitution | — |
395	| M7-T002 | Command registry: register KCA CLI subcommands declaratively | T001 |
396	| M7-T003 | Tool registry: tool metadata, approval policy labels, sandbox metadata | T001 |
397	| M7-T004 | Permission policy layer: allow/ask/deny resolution with structured JSON policy records | T003 |
398	| M7-T005 | Slash-style invocation: `kca skill run <name> [args] [--dry-run]` shows permissions + rendered prompt | T001, T004 |
399	| M7-T006 | Audit logging: record every tool execution in `agent_job_events` with policy decision | T004 |
400	| M7-T007 | Seed `.kca/skills/` with `run-milestone`, `triage-log`, `prepare-submission`, `review-pr` | T001 |
401	| M7-T008 | `tests/test_m7_smoke.py`: skill parsing, arg substitution, permission resolution, command registry, decision gates | T001–T006 |
402	| M7-T009 | Documentation: `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md` explaining Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs | all |
403	| M7-T010 | M7 exit criteria validation + `docs/m7-final-review.md` | all |
404	
405	### Permission policy design
406	
407	Runtime agent permissions are data, not ad-hoc prompts:
408	
409	```json
410	{
411	  "operation": "kaggle.submit",
412	  "default_decision": "ask",
413	  "reason": "External competition submission",
414	  "allowed_in_modes": ["human-approved", "competition-finalization"],
415	  "audit_required": true
416	}
417	```
418	
419	Allow by default: edit workspace files, run tests/benchmark, create artifacts,
420	summarize logs, call LiteLLM/local models, create branch, commit, create PR.
421	
422	Decision gate: submit to Kaggle, merge PR, publish dataset/kernel, apply
423	remote Supabase migration, spend above budget threshold, change model tier,
424	change competition direction/objective.
425	
426	Deny: read secrets, write outside workspace, sudo/root, rm outside workspace,
427	drop database/schema, force push, network exfiltration.
428	
429	### Recommended directory layout
430	
431	```text
432	.kca/
433	  skills/
434	    run-milestone/SKILL.md
435	    triage-log/SKILL.md
436	    prepare-submission/SKILL.md
437	    review-pr/SKILL.md
438	  tools/tools.yaml
439	  permissions/
440	    default.yaml
441	    permissive-dev.yaml
442	    competition-runner.yaml
443	
444	tools/kca/
445	  kca.py
446	  commands/
447	    job.py  skill.py  tool.py  decision.py
448	    workspace.py  kaggle.py  supabase.py
449	  agent/
450	    runner.py  skill_loader.py  tool_executor.py
451	    permission_policy.py  audit.py
452	```
453	
454	Exit criteria:
455	
456	- `kca skill list` shows available skills from `.kca/skills/`.
457	- `kca skill show <name>` prints parsed metadata and body.
458	- `kca skill run <name> ... --dry-run` prints planned tool permissions and rendered prompt without executing.
459	- Permission policy resolves allow/ask/deny for any (operation, mode) pair.
460	- Audit log records every tool execution with policy decision.
461	- `.github/workflows/` CI passes on main branch (no-db + lint at minimum).
462	- `tests/test_m7_smoke.py` passes without API keys or DB.
463	- Documentation explains Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs.

1	# Milestone Loop Protocol
2	
3	_Shared rules that apply to every milestone Loop Prompt (M0+) unless a
4	milestone explicitly overrides one._
5	
6	Each `docs/m*-loop-prompts.md` should reference this file once at the top
7	rather than duplicating the rules per prompt.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Sequencing
12	
13	- Loop Prompts within a milestone MUST execute in order.
14	- Each prompt's **acceptance checks MUST pass** before moving to the next.
15	- On failure: fix the specific issue and **retry that prompt only**; do
16	  not skip ahead and do not redo prompts that already passed.
17	
18	## 2. External systems and side effects
19	
20	- Do NOT call the **real Anthropic API or Kaggle API** outside of paths
21	  the milestone explicitly designates as live; default to `--dry-run`.
22	- Do NOT run real **Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload /
23	  model upload** unless the milestone explicitly requests it AND a
24	  human-approval record exists.
25	- Do NOT change **production Supabase**.
26	
27	## 3. Database validation
28	
29	- Use `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`
30	  — the `supabase-db` container on the local Docker network.
31	- Container IPs change on `docker compose down/up`; refresh with:
32	  ```bash
33	  docker inspect supabase-db \
34	    --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'
35	  ```
36	- DB calls and LAN-host calls require `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
37	  Cloud LLM calls stay **inside** the sandbox.
38	
39	## 4. Reporting
40	
41	- Report **PASS / FAIL / SKIP** inline for each prompt's verification
42	  step.
43	- At milestone end, write the milestone's defined **Closeout format**
44	  (see each milestone's last Loop Prompt for the exact fields).
45	
46	## 5. Git / GitHub — worktree mode
47	
48	This project executes each milestone inside a dedicated **git worktree**
49	branched off `main`.
50	
51	- **Mid-milestone, mid-prompt:** do not `git commit` or `git push`
52	  unless the individual task spec explicitly says so. Stage with
53	  `git add` and surface diffs in the inline report.
54	- **At milestone end** — once every Loop Prompt has PASSed and the
55	  milestone's Closeout has been written — Claude Code SHOULD:
56	  1. `git add` only the files listed in the Closeout's "files changed"
57	     section (or its equivalent).
58	  2. `git commit` using either:
59	     - one squash commit per milestone, OR
60	     - one commit per Loop Prompt,
61	     depending on the milestone's preference. The default is **one
62	     commit per Loop Prompt**, with the milestone's final review as the
63	     last commit.
64	  3. `git push` the worktree's branch to the remote.
65	  4. `gh pr create` against `main` using the milestone's
66	     `docs/m{N}-final-review.md` as the PR body.
67	
68	- The following **still require explicit human approval** at any time:
69	  - `git push --force` (any branch)
70	  - `gh pr merge` (any PR)
71	  - any push to `main` directly
72	  - any `gh label create/edit/delete`, `gh issue edit/comment`,
73	    `gh pr edit/comment` against issues or PRs **not** owned by this
74	    milestone
75	
76	- If the milestone's task spec or scope says
77	  "do not commit / push / open PRs", that override **wins** — typically
78	  used for planning-only or evidence-only milestones.
79	
80	## 6. Secrets and forbidden reads
81	
82	These are always denied, regardless of milestone:
83	
84	- `.env*`
85	- `**/kaggle.json`, `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`
86	- `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, any private key contents
87	- `~/.aws/**`, `~/.config/gcloud/**`
88	- `secrets/**`
89	
90	Shell commands that would surface the above (`cat`, `grep`, `head`,
91	`tail`, `less`, `more`, file uploads) over these paths are blocked at
92	the hook layer.
93	
94	---
95	
96	## How a milestone references this file
97	
98	In each Loop Prompt block, instead of repeating the rules above, include
99	one line near the top:
100	
101	```
102	Follow: docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md
103	```
104	
105	A milestone's `docs/m{N}-loop-prompts.md` should still spell out:
106	
107	- the milestone's own scope, non-goals, and task list;
108	- per-Loop-Prompt read lists, scope, acceptance criteria;
109	- any **override** of a default in this file (e.g. a planning-only
110	  milestone overriding the worktree commit/push behavior).
111	
````

# Kaggle Code Agent — Project State

_Last updated: 2026-05-24 (M9 exit)_

## Product intent
Build a hybrid human + AI competition engineering workbench. The first target is Kaggle-style competitions, with future support for authorized CTF/lab challenges. The system should research, discuss ideas with humans, edit code, run tests/evaluations, analyze results, iterate, and prepare submissions under human-approved guardrails.

## Chosen architecture direction
- Hybrid architecture.
- Claude Code Desktop/CLI for interactive project development and dogfooding (primary development tool for all layers).
- Claude Agent SDK for the production coding worker.
- Python-first worker for Kaggle/ML/CTF execution.
- TypeScript/Supabase control plane and UI shell (developed in Claude Code, not Lovable).
- GitHub + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations are the source of truth. All decisions, architecture, task specs, and safety rules live in repo files.
- Supabase is the control plane and audit database, not the primary code execution environment.

## Current MVP boundary
1. Local-first repository workflow with `CLAUDE.md`, skills, hooks, subagents, and GitHub.
2. Supabase schema for projects, sessions, jobs, messages, research notes, experiments, runs, submissions, artifacts, approvals, and `agent_tool_audit` (M8).
3. Kaggle baseline loop: understand competition, create validation, run baseline, record metrics, iterate, prepare submission.
4. Browser/research loop: fetch pages, summarize sources, track trust and citations.
5. Multi-agent reviewer gate + OTEL telemetry + local GPU model layer.
6. Authorized CTF sandbox loop only for explicit challenge environments.
7. Operator-facing UI: Dashboard, Run Timeline (OTEL swim-lane), Experiments, Research, Approval Inbox + Decision Gate, Artifact Browser.

## Human approval gates
Require approval for:
- Kaggle competition submissions.
- Kaggle kernel/notebook pushes.
- Any remote write operation.
- Any operation touching credentials, secrets, or account settings.
- Any CTF action outside a declared sandbox/challenge scope.
- PR merges (create is allowed, merge requires approval).

Mutations from the UI flow through `services/decision_api/` (FastAPI) →
`tools/kca/decisions.py` → DB. The browser bundle never holds a
Supabase service-role key. The M7 permission policy resolution stays
authoritative.

## Completed milestones
- **M0**: project baseline and memory discipline ✓
- **M1**: local Kaggle tooling wrapper baseline ✓
- **M2**: Supabase/control plane foundation ✓
- **M3**: Python-first competition worker v0 ✓
- **M4**: Kaggle competition workflow v0 ✓
- **M5**: research and browser workflow ✓
- **M6**: multi-agent review + OTEL telemetry + local-model layer ✓
- **M7**: KCA CLI architecture (command / skill / tool / permission policy) ✓
- **M8**: product UI shell + M7 follow-ups (audit table, schema gate, ToolSpec enforcement, decision_api) ✓
- **M8.5**: pre-M9 hardening — CI repair + GitHub Issues/PR/labels interface + M9 planning ✓
- **M9**: live end-to-end Kaggle regression test — Spaceship Titanic ✓

See `docs/m8-final-review.md` for M8 validation results (all 28 non-SKIP
checks PASS), `docs/m8_5-final-review.md` for the M8.5 roll-up (all 26
non-SKIP checks PASS; three PRs landed on `main` as #4, #5, #6), and
`docs/m9-final-review.md` for the M9 roll-up (30 PASS / 1 SKIP / 0 FAIL;
the SKIP is UI pnpm gates — M9 did not modify UI).

M9 metrics snapshot:
- LR baseline (M9-T002): CV accuracy **0.79144 ±0.0086** (5-fold stratified, seed=42).

## M9.4 at a glance

M9.4 closes the gap surfaced in the 2026-05-24 R3 meeting:

> 发现 Claude Code 有时执行任务时不够主动积极, 比如之前让其接手 legacy 的 kkr.py,
> kkr.yaml, 开始设计 build KCA 平台的 tool 时, agent 并没有询问原先设计中的一些理念,
> 比如多 Kaggle 账户提交。

The fix, per §6 of that note, is **not** "remind Claude to be more proactive."
It is **three role-isolated agents plus an acceptance gate** so proactivity
becomes a checkable artifact:

- `requirements-skeptic` — asks questions; never proposes implementation.
- `legacy-archaeologist` — reads legacy code/config; surfaces hidden design
  intent, multi-account / owner / env dimensions, side effects, registries.
- `design-red-team` — refutes the current proposed design; produces at least
  three alternatives and argues tradeoffs.

The three are wired together by a new `.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md`
that the milestone-loop-protocol invokes **before** any implementation work
begins on an architecture-shaped or legacy-migration-shaped task.

M9.4 is **planning + scaffolding**, not a feature-shipping milestone:

- New files land under `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/skills/`, `docs/architecture/`,
  `docs/tasks/`, and the milestone-loop-protocol gets one additive section.
- No `src/`, `tools/kca/`, `ui/`, `services/`, `supabase/migrations/` changes.
- No real Kaggle calls. No DB schema changes. No new permission policies.
- Validate by **dry-run replay** on `tools/legacy/kkr.py` + `tools/legacy/kkr.yaml`:
  the three agents must collectively recover the multi-account / owner / env
  semantics that were missed during the original migration.

### Entry gates

Direct entry into M9.4 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M9 is merged on `main` (`docs/m9-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS).
- The closing issue for M9.4 (TBD; analogous to issue #12 for M10) has
  `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`.
- `tools/legacy/kkr.py` and `tools/legacy/kkr.yaml` are reachable from the
  repo root — M9.4 uses them as the demonstration fixture.

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M9.4 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Question-only agent | `.claude/agents/requirements-skeptic.md` (new) | T001 |
| Legacy-reader agent | `.claude/agents/legacy-archaeologist.md` (new) | T002 |
| Refutation agent | `.claude/agents/design-red-team.md` (new) | T003 |
| Orchestration skill | `.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` (new) | T004 |
| Workflow hook | `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` — additive §7 "Discovery / Debate Gate" | T004 |
| Acceptance template | `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md` (new) — checkable AC list | T001 / T002 / T003 / T004 |
| Demonstration fixture | `docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/` — three agent transcripts replaying `kkr.py` migration | T005 |
| Smoke tests | `tests/test_m9_4_agents.py` — agent file parses, skill loader resolves, acceptance checks present | T005 |
| Final review | `milestone-final-review` skill | T006 |

### What's NOT in scope

- Building a runtime version of these agents inside `src/worker/`. M9.4 lives
  entirely in Claude Code's `.claude/` agent/skill surface. The runtime
  equivalent is a follow-up issue (separate milestone).
- Changing the existing `competition-researcher` / `evidence-reviewer` /
  `milestone-reviewer` agents. The three new agents are additive and
  role-isolated. Cross-references between them must be one-way and
  explicit.
- Adding new tools, permission policies, or DB rows for these agents.
  They use existing `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `WebFetch` (where applicable)
  and produce markdown output only.
- Auto-blocking implementation work via hook code. M9.4 enforces the
  Discovery / Debate Gate via **acceptance criteria** in task specs and
  the milestone-loop-protocol, not via a tool-level deny. Hook-based
  enforcement is a follow-up.
- Running the gate on every task. The gate is mandatory only for tasks
  the milestone explicitly tags as `arch:` or `legacy-migration:` in the
  task spec; routine task specs continue to use the existing protocol.

DB / sandbox details: M9.4 does not touch the DB. Sandbox bypass is **not**
required for M9.4 Loop Prompts unless the closeout step needs `git push` /
`gh pr create`; that follows the milestone-loop-protocol §5 default.

# M9.4-T003: `design-red-team` agent scaffold

## Milestone
M9.4: Discovery / Debate Gate agents (planning + scaffolding).

## Goal
Create `.claude/agents/design-red-team.md` — an agent that refutes a
proposed design. Given a task spec, ADR draft, or planning doc plus the
outputs of `requirements-skeptic` and `legacy-archaeologist`, the agent
must produce ≥3 alternative designs, surface capabilities the proposed
design would drop, and argue long-term costs. The agent does not
ratify designs and does not edit code.

Origin: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6 做法 3 (`design-red-team`).

## Read first

1. `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6
2. `docs/m9_4-loop-prompts.md` §"M9.4 at a glance"
3. `docs/tasks/M9_4-T001-requirements-skeptic.md`
4. `docs/tasks/M9_4-T002-legacy-archaeologist.md`
5. `docs/engineering-practice.md` — review-role precedent
6. `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` — skeptical, evidence-grounded precedent
7. `docs/adr/` — any existing ADR with an explicit
   "alternatives considered" section (front-matter precedent)

## Scope

1. Create `.claude/agents/design-red-team.md` with YAML front-matter:
   - `name: design-red-team`
   - `description:` proactive trigger before architecture / migration
     designs are accepted.
   - `tools: Read, Glob, Grep` — read-only. (No `Bash`. No `WebFetch`
     unless a later task explicitly adds it.)
   - `model: sonnet`.
   - `permissionMode: plan`.
   - No `skills:` line.
2. Body must define the four mandatory output sections:
   1. `alternatives:` — ≥3 alternative designs. Each entry: name,
      one-paragraph sketch, key tradeoff vs the proposed design.
   2. `dropped_capabilities:` — features / behaviors the proposed
      design would lose vs the legacy or vs the alternatives. Each
      entry MUST cite `file:line` evidence (per `CLAUDE.md` "Tone and
      style" — `file_path:line_number` pattern).
   3. `long_term_costs:` — cognitive load, ops burden, extensibility,
      blast radius. One sentence per axis minimum.
   4. `open_disagreements:` — explicit list of points where the
      red-team disagrees with the proposed design; each item ends
      with an actionable next step (more research, write a spike,
      ask human, defer to a follow-up issue).
3. Body must list Must NOT rules:
   - Do not sign off on a design ("the agent does not ratify, only
     refutes").
   - Do not modify code.
   - Do not file GitHub issues / PRs / comments.
   - Do not claim authority over the final decision — that belongs to
     the human.
4. Body must contain the checkable acceptance line: "Output MUST
   include ≥3 alternatives, ≥1 dropped capability with file:line
   evidence, all four long-term-cost axes, and ≥1 actionable
   open_disagreements entry."

````markdown
---
name: requirements-skeptic
description: Use proactively before implementation on architecture or legacy-migration tasks to surface hidden requirements via sharp questions. Asks; never proposes implementations.
tools: Read, Glob, Grep
model: sonnet
permissionMode: plan
---

You are a requirements skeptic. Your job is to interrogate a proposed task
or design *before any code is written*, so that hidden constraints,
forgotten personas, unstated side effects, missed edge cases, and
absent rollback plans become explicit. You ask questions — you do not
answer them.

This agent is paired with — but distinct from — `legacy-archaeologist`
(reads legacy artefacts) and `design-red-team` (refutes the proposed
design). Hand-off order is documented in
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` (M9.3): archaeology first,
skepticism second, red-team last. Acceptance criteria for all three
agents live in `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`.

## What you must do

Read the proposed task spec, any linked design doc / ADR / planning
prompt, and any legacy artefact the task touches. Produce a numbered
question list grouped by the five mandatory categories below. For each
question, name the consequence of leaving it unanswered (so the parent
session can prioritise).

Mandatory output categories:

1. `hidden_constraints` — limits, budgets, deadlines, licences, policy
   gates, compliance requirements, or dependencies the task spec does
   not name.
2. `personas_and_accounts` — every distinct human / service / Kaggle
   owner / GitHub identity / env-file mapping the task touches; cases
   where one persona is silently assumed.
3. `side_effects` — every remote / external write the task could
   trigger (Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload, GitHub

   semantics, idempotency, race conditions, version drift, empty /
   malformed input, very large input.
5. `rollback` — what proves the change can be reverted; what state
   would block a clean revert.

items you could not answer from the artefacts you read and that need a
human decision before implementation begins.

---
name: legacy-archaeologist
description: Use proactively before legacy-migration tasks to extract hidden design intent from legacy code, configs, READMEs, and notebooks. Reads only; never executes or modifies legacy artefacts.
tools: Read, Glob, Grep
model: sonnet
permissionMode: plan
---

You are a legacy archaeologist. Before any code that migrates,
replaces, or wraps a legacy artefact is written, you read that
artefact and produce a structured report of what it *does* and what
it *assumes*. The canonical failure mode you exist to prevent: the
`tools/legacy/kkr.py` / `kkr.yaml` migration missed multi-Kaggle-
account / owner / env semantics because no agent role was responsible
for surfacing them
(see `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6).

This agent is paired with — but distinct from — `requirements-skeptic`
(asks questions about the proposed task) and `design-red-team`
(refutes the proposed design). The hand-off order, when invoked via
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` (M9.3), is
archaeology → skepticism → red-team. Acceptance criteria for all
three agents live in `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`.

The `design-archaeology` *skill* (M9.3) and this *agent* are not the
same thing. The skill encodes a 10-section template that any session
can follow; this agent is the role-isolated subagent that produces
the report on demand, and whose tools / permission mode are
constrained so it cannot accidentally run the legacy code.

## What you must do

Read the named legacy artefacts (scripts, YAML / TOML / JSON configs,
READMEs, notebooks, accompanying dotenv example files). Produce a
report covering all ten mandatory sections below, in order. Each
section MUST cite `file:line` evidence — never a free-floating claim.

Mandatory output sections:

1. Workflows the legacy tool supports — the end-to-end flows a user
   could run (push / submit / watch / status / list / fetch /
   dry-run / verify / …). One bullet per workflow.
2. Hidden assumptions — environment variables, file-system layout,
   sentinel files, implicit ordering of operations, undocumented
   defaults, network reachability requirements.
3. User personas / owner accounts / env mappings — every distinct
   identity the artefact can act as (Kaggle owner, GitHub identity,
   service account, env-file slot). For each, name the config knob
   that selects it and where in the file it lives. This section is
   load-bearing for the kkr.py-style multi-account case.
4. Side effects — every remote / external write or read the artefact
   triggers (Kaggle pushes, dataset uploads, kernel pushes,
   filesystem writes outside the workspace, network egress).
5. State files / registries / dotenv overrides — every persistent
   thing the artefact reads or writes (manifest files, run
   registries, lock files, .env / .env.local / .env.<owner>).
6. Config dimensions — every CLI flag, env var, and YAML knob that
   changes behaviour. Include defaults.
7. Features to preserve — capabilities that the replacement MUST
   keep. Cite why (test coverage, audit obligation, user habit,
   compliance).
8. Features to deprecate — capabilities the replacement should drop,
   with reason (dead code, replaced by platform primitive, security
   risk, unmaintained dependency).
9. Questions that MUST be asked before implementation — handed off
   to `requirements-skeptic`. One bullet per question, with the
   evidence that triggered it.
10. Tests / fixtures that would prove behavior parity — what a
    `tests/test_<legacy>_parity.py` would have to cover so a
    migration cannot regress silently.

Acceptance line (the parent session checks this verbatim):

> Output MUST cover all 10 sections; ≥5 distinct legacy behavior
> dimensions must be named explicitly, including any multi-account /
> owner / env mapping the legacy artefact encodes.

## What you must NOT do

- Do not execute the legacy code. No `python kkr.py …`, no
  `kaggle …`, no shell invocation, no notebook execution. Your
  `permissionMode: plan` and read-only tool list already enforce
  this; treat it as load-bearing.
- Do not modify any legacy file. The artefact is evidence, not a
  workspace.
- Do not fetch external dependencies, install packages, or hit the
  network. Read what is on disk.
- Do not infer decisions from ambiguity. If two interpretations are
  equally plausible, name both in §9 (questions for skeptic) — do
  not pick one and present it as fact.

```

Return only this report. No prose preamble, no closing summary.

---
name: design-red-team
description: Use proactively before architecture or migration designs are accepted to refute the proposed approach with alternatives and dropped-capability analysis. Cites file:line; never ratifies.
tools: Read, Glob, Grep
model: sonnet
permissionMode: plan
---

You are a design red team. Given a proposed design (task spec, ADR
draft, planning doc) plus the upstream outputs from
`legacy-archaeologist` and `requirements-skeptic`, you refute the
proposal. You produce at least three alternative designs, name the
capabilities the proposal would drop, and argue the long-term costs.
You never approve a design. The human owns the decision; you make the
disagreement explicit.

This agent runs *last* in the Discovery / Debate Gate hand-off
(archaeology → skepticism → red-team), as documented in
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` (M9.3). The union of all
three agents' acceptance lines lives in
`docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`.

## What you must do

Read the proposed design plus the upstream archaeology and skeptic
reports. Produce a report with the four mandatory sections below.
Cite `file:line` evidence whenever you claim a capability would be
lost or a constraint would be violated — never a free-floating
assertion.

Mandatory output sections:

1. `alternatives:` — ≥3 alternative designs. Each entry MUST have a
   name, a one-paragraph sketch, and the key tradeoff vs the
   proposed design. Strawman alternatives (clearly weaker on every
   axis) do not count.
2. `dropped_capabilities:` — features / behaviours the proposed
   design would lose vs the legacy artefact OR vs any of the
   alternatives. Each entry MUST cite `file:line` evidence — the
   legacy file and line where the capability lives, or the
   alternative-design section where it would survive.
3. `long_term_costs:` — one sentence minimum per axis:
   - `cognitive_load` — how much a new contributor must hold in
     their head to use / change the design.
   - `ops_burden` — what breaks at 3am; what needs paging; what
     manual recovery looks like.
   - `extensibility` — how the design fares against the next two
     likely scope expansions (name them).
   - `blast_radius` — what fails if this design fails (data loss,
     leaderboard pollution, credential leak, audit gap).
4. `open_disagreements:` — explicit list of points where the
   red-team disagrees with the proposed design. Each item MUST end
   with an actionable next step: more research, write a spike, ask
   human, defer to a follow-up issue (with proposed labels).

Acceptance line (the parent session checks this verbatim):

> Output MUST include ≥3 alternatives, ≥1 dropped capability with
> file:line evidence, all four long-term-cost axes, and ≥1
> actionable `open_disagreements` entry.

## What you must NOT do

- Do not sign off on the design. The agent refutes; it does not
  ratify. Even if the design looks correct, your job is to surface
  the disagreement — emit an `open_disagreements: []` only if you
  have *exhausted* the search for one.
- Do not modify code, file GitHub issues / PRs / comments, or run
  shell commands. Your `permissionMode: plan` already refuses
  non-plan tool calls; treat that as load-bearing.
- Do not claim authority over the final decision. The human (or the
  parent session, with documented authority) owns the call.
- Do not invent file:line citations. If you cannot find evidence in
  the artefacts the upstream agents read, mark the claim as
  `evidence: unavailable` in §2 and route it to §4 as
  `open_disagreements`.

alternatives:

  2. ...
  3. ...

  - ...

long_term_costs:
  cognitive_load:    <one sentence>
  ops_burden:        <one sentence>
  extensibility:     <one sentence> — next likely scope: <two named expansions>
  blast_radius:      <one sentence>

open_disagreements:
  - <point of disagreement> — next step: <research | spike | ask-human | follow-up-issue [labels]>
  - ...
```

Return only this report. No prose preamble, no closing summary.

# Discovery / Debate Gate

_Status: M9.4 ships the gate (this doc + protocol §7 + the three agents). The
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` orchestration the gate
references is owned by M9.3; M9.3-T001 must land that skill before §7
becomes fully enforceable end-to-end._

## What this is

The Discovery / Debate Gate is the M9.4-shipped guardrail that turns
"please be more proactive in plan / design / architect mode" into a
**checkable artefact**. Three role-isolated subagents run before any
implementation work begins on an architecture-shaped or
legacy-migration-shaped task. Each agent has a canonical acceptance
line that the parent session verifies; the three lines together form
the gate.

Origin: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6 — the observation
that the original `tools/legacy/kkr.py` migration missed
multi-Kaggle-account / owner / env semantics because no agent role
was responsible for surfacing them.

## Agents

| Agent | File | Phase | Reads | Emits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `legacy-archaeologist` | `.claude/agents/legacy-archaeologist.md` | 1 of 3 | legacy artefacts (read-only) | 10-section archaeology report |
| `requirements-skeptic` | `.claude/agents/requirements-skeptic.md` | 2 of 3 | proposed task spec + archaeology report | numbered question list across 5 categories + `explicit_unknowns:` |
| `design-red-team` | `.claude/agents/design-red-team.md` | 3 of 3 | proposed design + archaeology + skeptic reports | ≥3 alternatives, dropped-capability evidence, 4 cost axes, open disagreements |

Hand-off order is **archaeology → skepticism → red-team**. Skipping a
phase is not allowed when the gate is mandatory (see §"When the gate
fires" below). The orchestration mechanism is
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` (owned by M9.3); until
that skill file is on disk, the gate runs by direct subagent
invocation against this doc.

## Acceptance lines (verbatim — union of all three agents)

A parent session verifies these three lines, byte-for-byte, against
the three agents' outputs. Failing any one of them means the gate
did not pass.

> Output MUST contain ≥5 questions spread across ≥3 categories, and
> an `explicit_unknowns:` section listing things the agent could not
> answer without human input.

> Output MUST cover all 10 sections; ≥5 distinct legacy behavior
> dimensions must be named explicitly, including any multi-account /
> owner / env mapping the legacy artefact encodes.

> Output MUST include ≥3 alternatives, ≥1 dropped capability with
> file:line evidence, all four long-term-cost axes, and ≥1
> actionable `open_disagreements` entry.

## When the gate fires

The gate is **mandatory** for any task whose spec carries one of the
two task tags in its `## Milestone` line, first heading, or front-matter:

- `arch:` — the task introduces or substantially revises an
  architectural primitive (worker, runner, sandbox, queue, telemetry
  pipeline, schema dimension, permission policy).
- `legacy-migration:` — the task migrates, rewrites, replaces, or
  takes over a legacy tool / config / notebook.

Routine tasks (bug fixes, doc edits, dependency bumps, small
refactors inside an existing primitive) do **not** trigger the gate.
The tag is added by the human authoring the task spec, not inferred
by an agent.

When the gate fires, the executing session MUST:

1. Invoke `legacy-archaeologist` first if the task touches any legacy
   artefact. (Skip for greenfield `arch:` tasks with no legacy code
   in scope.)
2. Invoke `requirements-skeptic` next, regardless.
3. Invoke `design-red-team` last, regardless.
4. Attach the three reports to the task closeout under
   `docs/evidence/<milestone>/<task>/discovery/`:
   - `legacy-archaeologist.md` (skip allowed only with explicit note)
   - `requirements-skeptic.md`
   - `design-red-team.md`
5. Verify all three acceptance lines (above) byte-for-byte against
   the reports. Failure to verify is a task-spec FAIL — not a vibe.

## Task tag convention

Tag placement options (any of these is acceptable; the parent session
should grep all three):

```markdown
## Milestone
M11.3: arch: new sandbox runner

# legacy-migration: M9.4-T002 legacy-archaeologist agent scaffold
```

or in YAML front-matter:

```yaml
tags: [arch, sandbox]
```

The tag is **opt-in by the task author** and reviewed by the human
who approves the task spec. M9.4 does not auto-attach tags.

## Closeout evidence path

```
docs/evidence/<milestone>/<task>/discovery/
  legacy-archaeologist.md
  requirements-skeptic.md
  design-red-team.md
```

`<milestone>` follows the existing convention (`m9_4`, `m10`, `m11_3`).
`<task>` follows the existing task-id convention
(`M9_4-T005-kkr-replay-and-smoke`, etc).

## Relationship to M9.3's `design-archaeology` skill

The skill in M9.3 encodes a 10-section archaeology *template* that any
session can run inline. The `legacy-archaeologist` agent in M9.4
emits the same 10-section report shape but in a role-isolated subagent
context: read-only tools, `permissionMode: plan`, no shell. Use the
skill for lightweight inline analysis; use the agent (via this gate)
when the task is large enough to warrant a separate subagent and a
gate-level acceptance check.

The two are deliberately compatible: the agent's output schema is a
strict subset of the skill's template, so a parent session can swap
between them without rewriting downstream consumers.

## Non-enforcement (M9.4 scope boundary)

M9.4 enforces the gate via **acceptance criteria** in task specs and
the milestone-loop-protocol §7 wording — not via tool-level denials
or hook-based blocks. Hook-based enforcement (e.g. a PreToolUse hook
that refuses `Edit` on `src/**` when an `arch:` task has no
`discovery/` evidence) is a deferred follow-up. File it as a separate
issue if you want it built.

## Cross-references

- Milestone protocol additive section: `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §7.
- M9.4 planning: `docs/m9_4-loop-prompts.md`.
- M9.3 skill (sibling milestone): `docs/m9_3-loop-prompts.md`,
  `.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` (M9.3-T001).
- Origin observation: `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6.

```markdown
# legacy-archaeologist report for tools/legacy/kkr.py + tools/legacy/kkr.yaml

Source: tools/legacy/kkr.py @ 6231fd1f54b6, tools/legacy/kkr.yaml @ 0543e71a5aa1

_Produced under the M9.4 Discovery / Debate Gate as the demonstration
replay (M9.4-T005). The agent body lives in
`.claude/agents/legacy-archaeologist.md`; this artefact is a manual
execution of that agent's protocol because the
`.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md` orchestration is owned by
M9.3-T001 and was not yet on disk at replay time._

## 1. Workflows supported

- `push <name>` — build a Kaggle notebook from `<code_file>` in
  `kkr.yaml`, push it as a Kaggle kernel under `<owner>/<slug>`.
  Entry: `kkr.py:2194`; main: `kkr.py:2293`; new-run impl:
  `_create_new_run` at `kkr.py:1511`.
- `submit [name]` — submit (a) a freshly built version or (b) an
  existing version selected by `NAME`, `--run`, or `--kernel/--version`.
  Entry: `kkr.py:2216`; existing-version path: `_submit_existing` at
  `kkr.py:1733`.
- `watch [name]` — poll remote kernel status until terminal.
  Entry: `kkr.py:2244`; impl: `_watch_impl` at `kkr.py:1943`.
- `fetch [name]` — download `source/output` artifacts for a selected
  run. Entry: `kkr.py:2267`; impl: `_fetch_impl` at `kkr.py:2006`.
- `status [name]` — one-shot remote-status query. Entry:
  `kkr.py:2272`; impl: `_status_impl` at `kkr.py:2074`.
- `list` — list tracked runs from the local registry. Entry:
  `kkr.py:2277`; row builder uses `_list_registry_entries` at
  `kkr.py:848`.

Cross-cutting flags on every subcommand: `--dry-run`, `--json`,
`--yaml`, `--run-root`, `--env`, `--quiet`, `-v/--verbose`
(`kkr.py:2158–2173`).

## 2. Hidden assumptions

- `kkr.yaml` has a `_base` block whose keys are merged with the
  per-config block via `_deep_merge` (`kkr.py:421–445`, validated at
  `kkr.py:491`). Per-config blocks override scalars and union-extend
  list-typed keys (`LIST_CFG_KEYS` at `kkr.py:60–66`).
- The `id` field MUST be `owner/slug`; `_slug_parts` at `kkr.py:466`
  raises if missing. Owner is derived from `id`, not specified
  independently — evidence: `kkr.py:520`.
- `_msg` template is `kkr@{ts}` by default (`kkr.py:514`,
  `_format_submit_message` at `kkr.py:551`), `{ts}` is filled at submit
  time, 500-character cap enforced at `kkr.py:558` — Kaggle rejects
  longer messages.
- `kkr.yaml` carries inline comments flagging two patches required
  against `kaggle==1.8.3`: one for `owner/model-slug` `model_sources`
  format (`kkr.yaml:31`), another to enable the H100 `docker_image`
  override (`kkr.yaml:38`). These patches are tribal knowledge — if the
  replacement does not preserve or supersede them, real pushes silently
  fail.
- Local registry root defaults to `.kkr/registry/` under
  `--run-root`; `--run-root` defaults to `DEFAULT_RUN_ROOT`
  (`kkr.py:2162`). Multiple concurrent runs on the same host all share
  one registry tree.

## 3. User personas / accounts / owners — load-bearing

This is the section the original migration missed (see
`docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6). The legacy tool *encodes*
multi-Kaggle-account submission as a first-class concept and the
replacement must not erase it.

- **`harrysun2006`** owner — see `kkr.yaml:7` `_base.id`, `kkr.yaml:58`
  (`a09h`), `kkr.yaml:77` (`b09h`), `kkr.yaml:90` (`c09h`),
  `kkr.yaml:108` (`d09h`). The `h` suffix in config names means "owned
  by harrysun2006".
- **`firefly2006`** owner — see `kkr.yaml:66` (`a09m`), `kkr.yaml:83`
  (`b09m`), `kkr.yaml:98` (`c09m`), `kkr.yaml:116` (`d09m`). The `m`
  suffix in config names means "owned by firefly2006".
- **`andreasbis`** owner — appears only in `kernel_sources` for `a09*`
  configs (`kkr.yaml:61, 69`) — i.e. a third-party kernel reused by
  both `h` and `m` flows. Not an active submission account, but an
  upstream code source the replacement must keep allowed.
- **Owner-to-env-file mapping** lives in `_load_env_for_owner` at
  `kkr.py:528–548`. Three resolution paths in order:
  1. `--env <path>` override — raises `FileNotFoundError` if the
     given path does not exist (`kkr.py:535–537, 547`).
  2. Programmatic `env_map[owner]` lookup (`kkr.py:538–539`).
  3. Fallback to `Path(".") / f".env.{owner}"` (`kkr.py:541`).
  Calling `load_dotenv(path, override=True)` (`kkr.py:543`) overrides
  any in-process Kaggle credentials, so back-to-back pushes under
  different owners work without an external account switcher.
- Selector aliases by suffix (`h` / `m`) are convention, not enforced
  by code. The replacement must either (a) preserve the convention and
  document it, or (b) introduce an explicit `owner:` field per config
  and migrate the YAML in place.

## 4. Side effects

- Kaggle kernel push: `_get_kaggle_api()` at `kkr.py:587` returns an
  authenticated `KaggleApi`; subsequent `kernels_push` / `kernels_status`
  / `kernels_output` invocations write to Kaggle servers under the
  owner currently loaded into the in-process credentials.
- Kaggle competition submit: chained off a successful push (see
  `_submit_existing` at `kkr.py:1733`); writes a competition submission
  under the current owner.
- Filesystem writes inside `--run-root` (default `.kkr/`):
  - `manifest.json` per run (`kkr.py:824–828`).
  - `registry/<run_id>.json` per run (`kkr.py:816, 838`).
  - Cached kernel outputs in `extracted_dirs` (`kkr.py:178`).
- `load_dotenv(..., override=True)` (`kkr.py:543`) mutates
  `os.environ` for the lifetime of the process. Long-running
  orchestrators must isolate.

## 5. State files / registries / dotenv overrides

- `.kkr/<run_dir>/manifest.json` — per-run `RunManifest`
  (`kkr.py:201–222`).
- `.kkr/registry/<run_id>.json` — `RegistryEntry`
  (`kkr.py:230–250`); driven by `_save_registry` (`kkr.py:838`) and
  `_list_registry_entries` (`kkr.py:848`).
- `.env`, `.env.{owner}`, or `<env_override>` — read by
  `_load_env_for_owner` (`kkr.py:528–548`). Treat `.env.{owner}` as a
  load-bearing schema, not an ad-hoc convention.
- File names: `DEFAULT_PUSH_FILENAME`, `DEFAULT_WATCH_FILENAME`,
  `DEFAULT_FETCH_FILENAME`, `DEFAULT_SUBMIT_FILENAME`
  (`kkr.py:43–46`) — used as legacy artifact filenames inside a run
  directory.

## 6. Config dimensions

Flag / env / YAML knobs that change behaviour. Defaults in parens.

- CLI (common, `kkr.py:2158–2173`):
  - `--yaml` (`kkr.yaml`), `--run-root` (DEFAULT_RUN_ROOT),
    `--env` (none → `.env.{owner}`), `--json` (false), `--dry-run`
    (false), `--quiet` (false), `-v/--verbose` (count).
- CLI (selector, `kkr.py:2174–2187`): `name` (positional),
  `--run`, `--kernel`, `--version`.
- CLI (push, `kkr.py:2197–2215`): `--stub`, `--wait`,
  `--interval` (DEFAULT_INTERVAL), `--timeout` (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT).
- CLI (submit, `kkr.py:2221–2243`): `--stub`, `--msg`, `--wait`
  (BooleanOptional, default False), `--interval`, `--timeout`.
- CLI (watch, `kkr.py:2249–2266`): `--wait` (BooleanOptional,
  default True), `--interval`, `--timeout`.
- CLI (list, `kkr.py:2282–2289`): `--limit` (50), `--refresh`.
- YAML knobs (`kkr.yaml:1–47`): `id`, `title`, `code_file`,
  `language`, `kernel_type`, `is_private`, `enable_gpu`,
  `enable_tpu`, `enable_internet`, `competition`, `submit_file`,
  `submit_type`, `competition_sources`, `dataset_sources`,
  `kernel_sources`, `model_sources`, `docker_image`,
  `machine_shape`, `_msg`, `_stub`, `_exts`, `_refs`,
  `_drop_tags`.

## 7. Features to preserve

- Multi-Kaggle-account / owner / env mapping (see §3). Why: the
  legacy YAML encodes 4 active configs per session (a/b/c/d in `h` and
  `m` variants), each routed to a different owner; the replacement
  cannot collapse this without breaking the established submission
  workflow. Evidence: `kkr.yaml:57–121`.
- `--dry-run` on every subcommand. Why: dry-run is the canonical
  smoke-test path; `_create_new_run` short-circuits at `kkr.py:1529`
  when `args.dry_run` is set.
- Stable JSON emission via `--json`. Why: downstream automation
  (`_emit_ok` at `kkr.py:332`) consumes shape; rename or reshape
  breaks any consumer.
- Local registry (`.kkr/registry/`). Why: replays, audit, and
  cross-day status queries depend on it; the platform should mirror
  this into the DB but keep a local copy for offline operation.
- Watch / status / fetch lifecycle. Why: Kaggle kernel runs are
  asynchronous and a successful submit can take minutes — polling
  must survive process restarts.
- `_deep_merge` semantics for `_base` + per-config (`kkr.py:421`).
  Why: list-union behaviour on `kernel_sources` / `model_sources`
  is relied on by every per-config block in `kkr.yaml`.

## 8. Features to deprecate

- The two `kaggle==1.8.3` patches flagged in `kkr.yaml:31, 38`. Why:
  the platform can pin a known-good `kaggle` version (or use the
  Kaggle Python API directly) and remove monkey-patching. Verify
  newer `kaggle` accepts `owner/model-slug` and `docker_image`
  fields natively before dropping.
- The `_exts` mechanism for run-extensions
  (`kkr.yaml:47` listing `kkr_simple`, `kkr_report`, `kkr_pycoll`;
  invoked at `kkr.py:122`). Why: bespoke per-run report shims have
  been superseded by the platform's `agent_reviews` + OTEL telemetry
  in M6; if any extension still has unique value, lift it into the
  platform as a tool, not a YAML knob.

## 9. Questions for `requirements-skeptic`

- Does the replacement expose an explicit `owner:` field, or does it
  inherit the `id: owner/slug` convention? Evidence: `kkr.yaml:7`,
  `kkr.py:466`.
- How does the replacement resolve credentials when multiple owners
  are active in one orchestration run? Evidence: `kkr.py:528–548`.
- Is `.env.{owner}` part of the public contract, or an implementation
  detail? Evidence: `kkr.py:541`.
- What happens to the `andreasbis/aimo-3-utils` kernel-source
  dependency if the replacement no longer supports cross-owner
  `kernel_sources`? Evidence: `kkr.yaml:61, 69`.
- Does the replacement preserve `--dry-run` semantics on every
  subcommand, or only on push/submit? Evidence: `kkr.py:1529, 1749`.

## 10. Parity tests

- `test_kkr_parity_push_dry_run` — invoke `push a09h --dry-run`,
  assert the plan JSON contains `owner=harrysun2006`,
  `slug=gpt-oss-120b-a09h`, and resolves `.env.harrysun2006` (or
  documented replacement). Fixture: a minimal `kkr.yaml`.
- `test_kkr_parity_owner_switch` — push `a09h` then `a09m`, assert
  the in-process credentials switched and that the second run did
  not inherit the first run's owner. Fixture: two-owner `kkr.yaml`.
- `test_kkr_parity_registry_roundtrip` — push, list, watch, fetch,
  assert one `RegistryEntry` per push with stable `run_id`.
- `test_kkr_parity_submit_message_cap` — supply a 600-char `_msg`,
  assert the replacement rejects with the same 500-char limit
  (`kkr.py:558`).
- `test_kkr_parity_dry_run_no_api_call` — patch the Kaggle API to
  raise on any call, assert dry-run completes without invoking it.
