# requirements-skeptic report for migrating tools/legacy/kkr.py into KCA

Source: tools/legacy/kkr.py @ 6231fd1f54b6, tools/legacy/kkr.yaml @ 0543e71a5aa1
Upstream: docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/legacy-archaeologist.md

_Produced under the M9.4 Discovery / Debate Gate (M9.4-T005). The agent
body lives in `.claude/agents/requirements-skeptic.md`; this artefact
is a manual execution of that agent's protocol against the proposed
KCA replacement of the legacy `kkr.py` flow._

## hidden_constraints

1. What is the maximum number of distinct Kaggle owners the replacement
   must support concurrently in one orchestration run? — consequence
   if unanswered: the replacement may pick a single-owner credential
   pattern (env vars set once at startup) and silently degrade the
   `harrysun2006` ↔ `firefly2006` dual-account workflow encoded in
   `kkr.yaml:57–121`.
2. Is `.env.{owner}` part of the public KCA contract, or an
   implementation detail the platform reserves the right to change? —
   consequence: if it's public, the KCA installer and onboarding docs
   need a documented `.env.<owner>` convention; if private, the
   platform owes users a migration path and a deprecation window.
3. Are `kaggle==1.8.3` monkey-patches (`kkr.yaml:31, 38`) still
   required against the version the platform pins, or are they
   superseded? — consequence: shipping the replacement without
   testing against the actually-pinned `kaggle` could silently break
   `model_sources` parsing or H100 `docker_image` overrides on first
   real push.
4. What is the maximum submission message length the replacement
   enforces? — consequence: legacy caps at 500 chars
   (`kkr.py:558`); a different cap downstream is a silent contract
   change.
5. Is the local registry (`.kkr/registry/`) the canonical state, or
   is the Supabase DB the canonical state with the local registry
   as a cache? — consequence: ambiguity here causes split-brain
   between offline-developed runs and platform-tracked runs.

## personas_and_accounts

1. The legacy tool encodes `harrysun2006` (`h` suffix) and
   `firefly2006` (`m` suffix) as distinct Kaggle owners and
   `andreasbis` as a kernel-source supplier (`kkr.yaml:7, 58, 66, 77,
   83, 90, 98, 108, 116, 61, 69`). Which of these survive in the
   replacement, with what role? — consequence: a single-owner
   replacement drops 50% of the live submission paths.
2. Does the replacement allow per-experiment owner override at the
   CLI, the way `--env <path>` overrides at `kkr.py:534–537`? —
   consequence: removing per-experiment override forces users to
   relaunch the platform between owner switches.
3. Are there additional Kaggle owners the user runs under not
   present in this committed `kkr.yaml`? — consequence: the
   archaeology may have under-counted because the YAML is committed
   but the actual `.env.*` files are gitignored.
4. Does the platform track which owner a given submission ran under
   in the `submissions` / `runs` table? — consequence: without an
   owner column the leaderboard-attribution audit trail breaks.
5. How does the platform reconcile a user being a GitHub identity, a
   Supabase user, AND a Kaggle owner — possibly with N:N mapping
   per project? — consequence: if the data model assumes 1:1, the
   multi-account case cannot be modelled at all.

## side_effects

1. Does the replacement preserve `--dry-run` on every subcommand, or
   only on push/submit? — consequence: dry-run gaps mean the smoke
   test path can't cover watch/fetch/status without hitting Kaggle.
2. The legacy `_load_env_for_owner` calls `load_dotenv(...,
   override=True)` at `kkr.py:543`, mutating `os.environ` in-process.
   Does the replacement isolate per-job credentials, or share the
   ambient environment? — consequence: shared env means one job can
   read the next job's secrets.
3. What reverses an accidental kernel push? — consequence: if the
   replacement does not surface a "delete-version" path,
   misconfigured pushes accumulate as draft versions Kaggle never
   garbage-collects.
4. What reverses an accidental competition submit? — consequence:
   Kaggle does not allow submission deletion; the platform must
   prevent rather than recover. Is the approval gate sufficient?
5. Where do `extracted_dirs` (`kkr.py:178`) land in the replacement?
   Inside the workspace, or in a platform-managed artifact store? —
   consequence: workspace bloat vs. unclear retention policy.

## edge_cases

1. What happens when a push starts under owner A and a credential
   switch happens mid-watch? — consequence: stale `KAGGLE_USERNAME`
   in the in-process env hits the wrong Kaggle account during
   status polling.
2. What happens if `_msg` formatting produces an empty string after
   trimming? — consequence: legacy raises at `_format_submit_message`
   only on >500 chars (`kkr.py:558`); empty `_msg` silently submits
   with `kkr@{ts}` default.
3. What happens if `kkr.yaml` has overlapping `kernel_sources`
   entries across `_base` and per-config? — consequence:
   `union_list` (`kkr.py:421`) deduplicates by simple equality;
   structured (dict) entries may not deduplicate as expected.
4. What happens during a partial registry write — process killed
   between `_save_manifest` and `_save_registry`? — consequence:
   orphaned manifest with no registry entry will not appear in
   `list`.
5. What happens if two concurrent `push` invocations allocate the
   same run id? — consequence: `_create_new_run` at `kkr.py:1511`
   uses `allocate=not args.dry_run` (`kkr.py:1523`); concurrent
   non-dry-run pushes may collide.

## rollback

1. If the replacement ships and a user wants to fall back to
   `tools/legacy/kkr.py`, is the legacy CLI still expected to work
   against the same `.kkr/registry/` directory? — consequence: if
   the registry schema is changed in flight, both tools see a
   broken registry.
2. Is the migration step idempotent? — consequence: re-running it
   after a partial failure should be safe.
3. Does the replacement write any state that the legacy CLI cannot
   ignore? — consequence: forward-incompatible additions silently
   poison rollback.
4. Is there an "export to legacy YAML" path for emergency rollback?
   — consequence: without it, the only fallback is the last commit
   of `kkr.yaml`, which loses any per-experiment edits made through
   the platform.
5. What is the rollback gate: a CLI command, a feature flag, a
   redeploy, or an out-of-band manual procedure? — consequence:
   ambiguity here means rollback during an incident is slow.

## explicit_unknowns

- Whether the `harrysun2006` / `firefly2006` owners are still active
  Kaggle accounts (cannot be inferred from the committed YAML
  alone — see memory `reference_supabase_db` for unrelated
  authoritative-config patterns).
- Whether `andreasbis/aimo-3-utils` is a permanently public Kaggle
  utility kernel or a moving target.
- Whether the H100 `docker_image` `gcr.io/kaggle-private-byod/...`
  (`kkr.yaml:39`) requires special Kaggle account whitelisting; the
  comment "可以 patch kaggle 1.8.3, 来使用 H100 GPU" hints at it but
  doesn't confirm.
- Whether the replacement is expected to support `submit_type:
  local` (CSV submit) AND `submit_type: notebook` (kernel push)
  through the same code path, or split per ADR-0009 / M10.
- Whether the platform's `kca kaggle push` (M10) is intended to
  *replace* `kkr.py push` or to *co-exist* with it during
  transition.

```

# design-red-team report for the KCA replacement of `tools/legacy/kkr.py`

Source: tools/legacy/kkr.py @ 6231fd1f54b6, tools/legacy/kkr.yaml @ 0543e71a5aa1
Upstream archaeology: docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/legacy-archaeologist.md
Upstream skeptic:     docs/evidence/m9_4-kkr-replay/requirements-skeptic.md

_Produced under the M9.4 Discovery / Debate Gate (M9.4-T005). The
agent body lives in `.claude/agents/design-red-team.md`; this
artefact is a manual execution of that agent's protocol. The
"proposed design" being refuted is the current M9 / M10 trajectory
that absorbed `kkr.py`'s push/submit semantics into `tools/kca/kg.py`
(via `cmd_push`, `cmd_submit`) without an explicit multi-owner
contract._

## alternatives

1. **Owner-as-first-class field in `RunSpec`.** Introduce an explicit
   `owner: str` field on the platform's run/experiment record and on
   every CLI subcommand (`kca kaggle push --owner harrysun2006 ...`).
   Resolve credentials by looking up a Supabase-managed
   `kaggle_credentials` table keyed by `(project_id, owner)`. Sketch:
   the CLI passes `owner` through to a worker; the worker loads the
   matching credential set into a short-lived per-job environment
   (no `os.environ` mutation). Key tradeoff vs proposal: adds one
   schema column and one Supabase RLS path, but eliminates ambient
   credential state and makes "which owner pushed this kernel" a
   queryable fact rather than a log artefact. Closest legacy
   evidence: `kkr.py:528–548` (per-owner env), `kkr.py:520` (owner
   derived from `id`).

2. **Per-job dotenv subprocess isolation.** Keep the
   `.env.{owner}` convention from `kkr.py:541`, but run each
   Kaggle-touching subcommand in a fresh subprocess with only the
   selected dotenv loaded, instead of mutating the parent process's
   `os.environ` (`kkr.py:543`). Sketch: `kca` shells out to a small
   `kaggle-runner` subprocess; the parent never sees credential
   state. Key tradeoff vs proposal: zero schema change, lower risk
   of credential bleed between concurrent jobs, but adds
   per-subcommand fork overhead and makes long-running watch loops
   slightly harder to instrument with the platform's OTEL spans
   (`agent_telemetry_spans` from M6).

3. **Credential-scoped tool wrappers via the M7 permission policy.**
   Treat `kaggle_submit(owner)` and `kernel_push(owner)` as separate
   operations in `.kca/permissions/*.yaml` (M7 policy layer), each
   with its own `allow/ask/deny` resolution and its own audit row.
   Sketch: tools never directly read credentials; the permission
   layer materialises a short-lived credential token per call.
   Key tradeoff vs proposal: tightest audit story (every owner-scoped
   external write is a distinct permission decision), at the cost
   of expanding the M7 policy surface from one Kaggle-write operation
   to N (one per active owner) and requiring policy authors to
   enumerate owners in advance. Closest legacy evidence:
   `kkr.py:587–595` (single ambient `KaggleApi`).

## dropped_capabilities

- **Multi-account submission via suffix convention.** The legacy
  `kkr.yaml` runs four config families (a/b/c/d) each in `h` /
  `m` variants, routing to `harrysun2006` and `firefly2006`
  respectively. The current platform trajectory has no explicit
  owner field on its run record; absorbing `kkr.py push/submit`
  into `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push` without §3's owner-as-first-class
  field silently collapses this to a single owner. Evidence:
  `tools/legacy/kkr.yaml:57–121` (every per-config block declares
  its own `id: owner/slug`); `tools/legacy/kkr.py:520` (owner
  parsed from `id`); `tools/legacy/kkr.py:528–548` (owner-keyed
  env-file resolution). Survives in: alternative 1, alternative 2,
  alternative 3, legacy.
- **Per-experiment `--env <path>` override.** Legacy CLI allowed
  overriding the dotenv path on a single invocation
  (`tools/legacy/kkr.py:535–537`). The proposed `kca kaggle push`
  signature (per `docs/m10-loop-prompts.md` "What's in scope") does
  not expose a `--env` flag. Evidence: `tools/legacy/kkr.py:2165`.
  Survives in: alternative 2, legacy.
- **`kernel_sources` cross-owner reuse.** Legacy YAML can reference
  another owner's kernel (`andreasbis/aimo-3-utils`) as a build
  source. Evidence: `tools/legacy/kkr.yaml:61, 69`. Survives in:
  legacy, alternative 1 (with an explicit
  `cross_owner_kernel_sources` allow-list); not yet wired into
  alternative 3.
- **Stable JSON shape for `--json` output.** Legacy `_emit_ok` at
  `tools/legacy/kkr.py:332` and `_emit_fail` define a contract many
  ad-hoc scripts depend on. The platform's `kca kaggle push --json`
  emits a different shape (an `experiment_runs` row). Evidence:
  unavailable in the current branch — route to `open_disagreements`.

## long_term_costs

cognitive_load:    Without an explicit owner field, every new
                   contributor must read `_load_env_for_owner` to
                   understand that `kca kaggle push` silently picks a
                   credential from `os.environ` and that the
                   `.env.<owner>` filesystem schema is load-bearing.
                   Alternative 1 trades that for one schema column
                   and one CLI flag.
ops_burden:        Ambient-credential failures look like "the wrong
                   account submitted" — a 3am page that requires
                   reading audit logs to reconstruct. Alternative 2
                   reduces this to "subprocess exited 1"; alternative
                   3 surfaces it as a denied permission policy
                   resolution before any external write.
extensibility:     Next likely scope expansions: (a) a third Kaggle
                   account for a teammate, (b) per-owner Kaggle API
                   throttling (Kaggle's rate limits are per-owner,
                   not per-IP). The current trajectory needs a code
                   change to absorb (a); alternative 1 needs a row
                   insert. Neither (a) nor (b) is easy on the
                   current trajectory because owner is not modelled
                   at all.
blast_radius:     Worst case on the current trajectory: a job
                   intended for `firefly2006` pushes to
                   `harrysun2006` because the ambient env was set
                   by the previous job. That kernel push goes on
                   the wrong leaderboard, may consume the other
                   account's daily-submission quota, and the
                   `submissions` row has no field to record which
                   owner ran it. Alternatives 1 and 3 prevent this
                   structurally; alternative 2 prevents it via
                   subprocess isolation.

## open_disagreements

- The current M10 plan accepts the proposed
  `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push` without an explicit owner contract.
  Disagree — next step: open a follow-up issue
  (labels: `area:kaggle`, `type:feature`, `policy:approval-required`)
  to add an `owner` field on `runs` / `experiment_runs` and a
  `--owner` flag on `kca kaggle push` / `kca kaggle submit` before
  the next live kernel-push milestone after M10.
- The `--env <path>` override is not in the M10 scope. Disagree —
  next step: ask human whether `.env.<owner>` is the public
  contract (in which case `--env <path>` is the documented escape
  hatch) or an implementation detail (in which case the platform
  owes a migration to a credentials table).
- The `_msg` 500-char cap and the `{ts}` template are not
  re-documented in the M10 spec. Disagree — next step: spike a
  parity test (`tests/test_kkr_submit_message_cap`) that exercises
  the cap against `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit` before M11.
- The legacy `_emit_ok` / `_emit_fail` JSON shape may have
  consumers outside this repo. Disagree — next step: research the
  JSON-shape contract (grep for `kkr_push.json`, `kkr_watch.json`
  filename literals in any sister repo); defer to a follow-up
  issue if a real consumer is found.
- The `kaggle==1.8.3` monkey-patch dependency is hidden tribal
  knowledge. Disagree — next step: write a smoke test against the
  pinned `kaggle` version (in `tests/test_kaggle_version_smoke.py`)
  that asserts `owner/model-slug` parsing and `docker_image`
  field acceptance work without patches; if it fails, the
  knowledge becomes a test failure rather than a silent push
  failure.

```

"""M9.4 Discovery / Debate Gate — smoke tests.

No DB, no creds, no network. Verifies:
- the three .claude/agents/*.md files parse with required front-matter;
- docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md exists and contains the
  union of all three agents' canonical acceptance lines as substrings;
- docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md has an additive §7 heading;
- at least one M9.4-T005 evidence transcript names the multi-account /
  owner / env mapping the legacy kkr migration originally missed.

The .claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md skill resolves are
*optional* at M9.4 close-time — M9.3-T001 owns shipping that file. The
test skips that assertion if the skill is not present, marking it
xfail-like to surface the dependency without failing the M9.4 milestone.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
import yaml

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

AGENT_FILES = [
    REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "agents" / "requirements-skeptic.md",
    REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "agents" / "legacy-archaeologist.md",
    REPO_ROOT / ".claude" / "agents" / "design-red-team.md",
]

REQUIRED_FRONTMATTER_KEYS = {"name", "description", "tools", "model", "permissionMode"}

ACCEPTANCE_LINES = {
    "requirements-skeptic": (
        "Output MUST contain ≥5 questions spread across ≥3 categories, and "
        "an `explicit_unknowns:` section listing things the agent could not "
        "answer without human input."
    ),
    "legacy-archaeologist": (
        "Output MUST cover all 10 sections; ≥5 distinct legacy behavior "
        "dimensions must be named explicitly, including any multi-account / "
        "owner / env mapping the legacy artefact encodes."
    ),
    "design-red-team": (
        "Output MUST include ≥3 alternatives, ≥1 dropped capability with "
        "file:line evidence, all four long-term-cost axes, and ≥1 "
        "actionable `open_disagreements` entry."
    ),
}

EVIDENCE_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "evidence" / "m9_4-kkr-replay"


def _split_frontmatter(text: str) -> tuple[dict, str]:
    parts = text.split("---", 2)
    assert len(parts) >= 3, "missing YAML front-matter delimiters"
    meta = yaml.safe_load(parts[1])
    assert isinstance(meta, dict), "front-matter is not a YAML mapping"
    return meta, parts[2]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", AGENT_FILES, ids=lambda p: p.name)
def test_agent_frontmatter_parses(path: Path) -> None:
    assert path.exists(), f"missing agent file: {path}"
    meta, _ = _split_frontmatter(path.read_text())
    missing = REQUIRED_FRONTMATTER_KEYS - set(meta)
    assert not missing, f"{path.name} missing front-matter keys: {missing}"
    assert meta["permissionMode"] == "plan", (
        f"{path.name} must declare permissionMode: plan (read-only role)"
    )


def _normalise_blockquote(text: str) -> str:
    """Collapse blockquote line-wraps so a multi-line acceptance line
    can be matched as a single substring."""
    return re.sub(r"\n> ?", " ", text)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "path,key",
    [(p, p.stem) for p in AGENT_FILES],
    ids=lambda v: v.name if isinstance(v, Path) else v,
)
def test_agent_has_canonical_acceptance_line(path: Path, key: str) -> None:
    expected = ACCEPTANCE_LINES[key]
    haystack = _normalise_blockquote(path.read_text())
    assert expected in haystack, (
        f"{path.name} is missing its canonical acceptance line"
    )


def test_discovery_debate_gate_doc_present() -> None:
    doc = REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "architecture" / "discovery-debate-gate.md"

    text = _normalise_blockquote(doc.read_text())
    for key, line in ACCEPTANCE_LINES.items():
        assert line in text, (
            f"discovery-debate-gate.md missing {key}'s acceptance line"
        )
    assert "arch:" in text and "legacy-migration:" in text, (
        "discovery-debate-gate.md must document both task tags"
    )
    assert "docs/evidence/<milestone>/<task>/discovery/" in text, (
        "discovery-debate-gate.md must document the evidence path"
    )

    )
